question: What does 'variance' mean?
answer: Variance is a measure of how much the values in a dataset vary from the mean. [S4] In statistics, variance quantifies the spread of a dataset [S1] [S4].

citations.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
citations.text: 1. Descriptive Statistics Descriptive statistics summarize a dataset. Measures of central tendency are the mean (the sum of the values divided by the number of values), the median (the middle value of the sorted data) and the mode (the most frequent value). The mean is sensitive to outliers; the median is robust to them. For right-skewed data such as incomes the mean is usually larger than the median. Measures of spread describe variability. The range is maximum minus minimum. The variance averages squared deviations from the mean, and the standard deviation is the square root of the variance, so it has the same units as the data. The interquartile range (IQR) is Q3 minus Q1 and is used to flag outliers: a common rule marks values below Q1 - 1.5 * IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 * IQR. citations.title: Statistics Estimators And Bias
citations.text:
2. Variance of an Estimator
The variance of an estimator describes how much the estimate changes from one random sample
to the next. For the sample mean it equals sigma squared divided by n, so the standard error of the
mean is sigma divided by the square root of n.
This is not the same quantity as the variance of the data themselves, which describes the spread
of individual observations around their mean. Quadrupling the sample size halves the standard
error but does not change the variance of the data.

Sample  variance divides by n - 1 (Bessel's correction) because deviations are measured from the sample mean rather than the unknown population mean, which would otherwise underestimate the true variance. Use sample variance whenever the data are a sample used to estimate a larger population.

S3.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S3.text:
2. Variance in Machine Learning
In machine learning the variance of a model is how much its predictions change when it is trained
on different training sets drawn from the same source. High-variance models such as deep
decision trees fit the quirks of one training set. This is a property of the learning algorithm, not the
spread of a data column.
The spread of a feature column is a different matter. In scikit-learn VarianceThreshold removes
features whose variance is below a threshold; the default threshold is 0.0, which removes only
constant features.

S5.title: Statistics Reference Notes
S5.text:
DESCRIPTIVE FORMULAS
Mean: x-bar = (sum of x) / n
Population variance: sigma^2 = sum((x - mu)^2) / N
Sample variance: s^2 = sum((x - x-bar)^2) / (n - 1)
Standard deviation: the square root of the variance.
IQR = Q3 - Q1. Outlier fences: Q1 - 1.5*IQR and Q3 + 1.5*IQR.
Coefficient of variation: CV = standard deviation / mean.
